content: The test image shows a corn ear with white/gray mold growing on and between kernels. The mold appears whitish-gray, the kernels are yellow, and the husks look bleached/dried. This points toward an ear rot. Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Diplodia** (white mold from base, bleached husks), **Ear_rots_Gibberella** (pinkish mold at tip), **Fusarium** (white to pink scattered mold).

Looking at the comparison:

- **Diplodia reference**: Dried, mummified brownish kernels covered in white mold — more advanced stage than the test image
- **Gibberella reference**: Shows mainly dark husk lesions — doesn't match
- **Fusarium reference**: Yellow kernels with white/pinkish mold on clustered/scattered kernels — similar but mold appears more pink/salmon

The test image shows yellow, still-plump kernels with white/gray mold growing between and over kernels in patches along the ear, with bleached husks. This is most consistent with **Ear_rots_Diplodia** — the white mold appearance, coverage over and between kernels, and bleached husk tissue all align. The yellow kernels suggest an earlier/mid stage before full mummification. No pink/red tint rules out Gibberella; no starburst pattern rules out Fusarium.
